checks.evidence: Every S-01–S-24 source reference resolves to K-001–K-033; architecture is fixed to 99f6f02, market data is dated 2026-08-18, and enterprise conclusions are labeled as public-evidence assessment.

SEC-01 asks four questions; SEC-02/03 explain control, composition, state, interfaces, and Plugin boundaries; SEC-04 separates primitives from enterprise evidence; SEC-05 maps market layers; SEC-06 closes with reproducible study.
All 24 slides have a unique purpose, takeaway, and conclusion-led title; S-04, S-12, S-16, and S-20 serve only as section transitions.
Body content is capped at five items per slide and spatial visuals carry mechanism detail; body type remains at least 17 pt.
Every slide specifies an executable visual kind; diagrams, state machines, matrices, and section compositions directly support their takeaways.
Circuit Atlas scores 94, ahead of Open Source Editorial at 86 and Enterprise Blueprint at 81, because native diagrams best encode runtime, lifecycle, boundary, and market relationships.
Every slide uses style_version 1, a defined layout, and light/dark/signal variants; all narrative artifacts use design_version 2.
The system uses 16:9, 0.55 in safe margins, a 12-column grid, 0.36 in block gaps, 30–42 pt titles, 17–23 pt body, and 9–12 pt captions.
Variant contrast passes deterministic thresholds; non-decorative visuals have alt text; risk and state use labels and shape in addition to color.
Both designs use native PowerPoint shapes, diagrams, and tables only, with no external photos, icons, screenshots, or AI assets.
All content and summary slides reference valid K-* items and reserve footer space for compact sources, fixed commit, retrieval date, and evidence limits.
Twenty-one layouts, three variants, complete tokens, and slide-level visual, note, citation, and alt-text instructions are sufficient for ppt-master implementation.
